entries.name: Devil Fruit Creation
entries.text:
When a character consumes a Devil Fruit, they gain supernatural abilities almost immediately. However, this newfound power comes at a steep cost: a profound vulnerability to seawater and seastone. Though all Devil Fruit users share these core weaknesses, some fruits may also carry additional unique vulnerabilities.
The Expanded Devil Fruit Encyclopedia serves as a foundational guide for Dungeon Masters seeking to design or adapt Devil Fruits for their campaign. While you are free to homebrew, the Encyclopedia provides a reliable structure for creation. Typically, Paramecia users draw spells from any class, Zoan users undergo beast-like transformations similar to druids, and Logia users combine spellcasting with transformative elemental abilities. This design approach ensures Devil Fruits fit naturally within the structure of standard D&D 5e, much like magic items.

sections.name: Step 1: Category & Appearance
sections.text:
Begin by marking the name of the Devil Fruit, its rarity (Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, or Legendary), its type (Paramecia, Zoan, or Logia), and its subtype. For example, the Hie Hie no Mi (Ice Fruit) would be categorized as a Solid Logia. Then, provide a brief description of its abilities according to its type.
Each Devil Fruit also features a unique and peculiar physical appearance. Describe its shape, colors, and the patterns decorating it. These whimsical designs add character to each fruit and hint at their latent power.
Example: Bara Bara no Mi (Dividing)

rows: Devil Fruit, Uncommon Type. Body Enhancer Paramecia Description. Can split and
divide parts of your body into pieces and can control said
pieces telekinetically. Fruit appearance Dark red berries

sections.name: Step 2: Weaknesses
sections.text: With great power comes great vulnerability. All Devil Fruit users inherit three universal weaknesses:

sections.name: Standing Water
sections.text:
A Devil Fruit user’s swimming speed is reduced to 0. If the user is more than half-submerged in standing water (fresh or salt water) or within 20 feet of a shoreline while submerged in water, they become incapacitated. While incapacitated, they cannot use Devil Fruit features or maintain active Devil Fruit spells.
If fully submerged, they begin sinking according to the armor they wear (5 ft./round for light armor, 10 ft./round for medium armor, 15 ft./round for heavy armor). A submerged user may hold their breath for 1 + Constitution modifier in minutes (minimum 30 seconds). Upon drowning, they fall to 0 HP and can survive only a few rounds before dying unless stabilized.

sections.name: Seastone
sections.text: Physical contact with seastone requires the user to succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw each round or become incapacitated for that turn. Whether they succeed or fail, the user cannot use Devil Fruit features while in contact with seastone.

sections.name: One Devil Per Body
sections.text: A creature can only ever have one Devil Fruit. Consuming a second causes immediate death as the body violently rejects the conflicting powers. Revival by certain spells (such as Wish or True Resurrection) removes all Devil Fruit powers permanently.

sections.name: Optional Weakness: Natural Counter
sections.text:
Additionally, individual fruits may have optional vulnerabilities fitting their theme. For instance, a fruit that generates oil may be vulnerable to fire.
Example: Bara Bara no Mi (Dividing)

sections.name: Step 3: Strengths and Features
sections.text:
Upon consuming a Devil Fruit, a user quickly becomes aware of its core strengths and abilities. These features vary greatly based on the fruit’s type and are detailed further in their respective sections.
Even the simplest Devil Fruits should offer unique gameplay options. Consider resistances, immunities, or unusual movement features when designing your fruit’s strengths.
Some Devil Fruit features require a target to make a saving throw or involve spell attack rolls. Instead of using a traditional ability modifier, Devil Fruits use Willpower (see Chapter 5: Spirit Surges) for determining DCs and attacks. The calculations are as follows:
Devil Fruit save DC = 10 + half of your Willpower (rounded up)
Devil Fruit Attack Modifier = 2 + half of your Willpower (rounded up)
Example: Bara Bara no Mi (Dividing)

damage, as your body can divide to avoid sharp objects.
Floating Limbs. You can use the Mage Hand cantrip.
Additionally, when you make a melee attack on your turn,
your reach for it is 30 feet greater than normal.

sections.name: Step 4: Devil Fruit Spells, Skills, and Charges
sections.text:
Devil Fruits grant users a number of “charges” used to fuel spells or special abilities tied to their fruit’s nature. Expended charges are replenished daily at dawn.
You can find examples of scaling for each fruit type in their rules sections.
Example: Bara Bara no Mi (Dividing)

Carnival). You can expend 1 or more of this fruits charges to
cast one of the following spells from it without needing to
blur (2 charges), kinetic jaunt (2 charges). The devil fruit
regains expended charges daily at dawn.

sections.name: NPC Devil Fruit Charges
sections.text: Instead of trying to scale creatures with player level rules as seen in their respective sections, consider giving your NPCs a static amount of charges to make your life easier.

sections.name: Step 5: Devil Fruit Advancement and Awakening
sections.text:
As players grow in strength, so too do their Devil Fruits. At higher levels, fruits “Awaken,” unlocking greater power often breaking their earlier limitations. Awakenings typically allow casting a powerful, high- level spell once per day without expending charges. See Chapter 5: Spirit Surges for more information.

entries.name: Paramecia Rules
entries.text: Paramecia Devil Fruits are one of the three primary classifications of Devil Fruits. They grant users a wide range of superhuman abilities, usually by altering their bodies, producing substances, or modifying the environment around them. This section provides detailed guidance for designing and understanding Paramecia-type Devil Fruits.

sections.name: Paramecia Subtypes
sections.text:
Each Paramecia Devil Fruit belongs to one of three subtypes: Body Enhancer, Substance Generator, or Environment Alterer. You must select one subtype when creating a Paramecia Devil Fruit, as this defines the core nature of the abilities it grants. Only through Awakening can users transcend these initial limitations.
For example, the Toge Toge no mi (Spike Paramecia) could classify as either a “body enhancer” or “environment alterer” subtype, allowing you to either make your body spiky or make the area around you spiky. However, you must pick only one of these two subtypes before continuing to develop the rest of your abilities. The only exception to this rule is if you “awaken” your devil fruit powers later on, which will give you the ability to bypass the limitations of your paramecia subclass.

sections.name: Paramecia Type: Body Enhancer
sections.text:
Body Enhancers alter their own bodies and clothing, often reshaping, stretching, or hardening themselves. They commonly use spells from the schools of Transmutation, Illusion, or Abjuration.
For example, the Bara Bara no Mi allows the user to split their body into independent floating parts.

sections.name: Paramecia Type: Substance Generator
sections.text:
Substance Generators produce a specific material from their bodies, using it for offense, defense, or battlefield control. Their abilities often align with Evocation, Conjuration, or Abjuration magic.
The Doku Doku no Mi, for instance, lets its user create and manipulate poisonous substances.

sections.name: Paramecia Type: Environment Alterer
sections.text:
Environment Alterers modify the properties of objects, creatures, or even entire areas. They frequently draw on spells from Enchantment, Necromancy, Illusion, Transmutation, or Divination.
An example is the Noro Noro no Mi, which slows the movement of targets within its area of effect.

sections.name: Paramecia Damage Types, Resistances, and Immunities
sections.text:
Paramecia users often develop resistances or immunities related to their Devil Fruit’s nature. These should be selected carefully in collaboration with the Dungeon Master to ensure they fit thematically. For instance, a rubber-based user might gain immunity to lightning and nonmagical bludgeoning damage.
In some cases, spells must be modified to match the fruit’s abilities. For example, a Devil Fruit that produces acid might alter a spell like Cone of Cold to instead deal acid damage.
It is important to note that magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage (such as that inflicted by Armament Haki) bypasses any resistances or immunities granted by Devil Fruits.

sections.name: Paramecia Basic Skills
sections.text:
Every Paramecia user gains an innate “basic skill” that can be used freely while they are not incapacitated or exposed to seawater or seastone. Basic skills are often represented by at-will abilities or cantrips.
For example, the Bara Bara no Mi user can extend their melee reach by 30 feet, while the Gomu Gomu no Mi enhances flexibility and resilience.
If a basic ability proves too powerful for unlimited use, it may instead be limited to a number of uses per day, refreshing at dawn.
Generally, Uncommon and Rare Devil Fruits should be more cautious with granting limitless abilities, while Very Rare and Legendary Devil Fruits can justify offering more potent basic powers.
The example sheet below shows an early design idea for the Nuke Nuke no Mi using paramecia immunities and resistances as well as basic skills.

sections.name: Paramecia Spells, Skills, and Scaling
sections.text:
Paramecia users gain access to spells and abilities tied to their fruit’s theme. Spells may be selected from any official 5e class list, but they must fit the subtype and nature of the Devil Fruit. Additionally, the maximum spell level available is determined by the user’s character level and fruit rarity.

sections.name: Paramecia Awakening
sections.text:
As Paramecia users grow stronger, they may eventually unlock the power of Awakening. This allows them to transcend the initial limitations of their fruit’s subtype and gain new, transformative powers.
Typically, an Awakening grants a single, high-impact ability that allows the user to manipulate their environment in ways previously impossible. Awakening features often bypass normal charge limits or provide access to higher-level spells.
An example is the Nuke Nuke no Mi, which upon Awakening allows the user to cast Etherealness once per day without using any charges.

entries.name: Zoan Rules
entries.text: Zoan Devil Fruits are one of the three primary classifications of Devil Fruits. They grant users the ability to transform into specific animals, ancient creatures, or mythical beasts, depending on the fruit’s rarity. While the transformation grants incredible physical capabilities, Zoan users balance their newfound strength with the same vulnerabilities as all Devil Fruit users.

sections.name: Zoan Subtypes
sections.text:
Each Zoan Devil Fruit falls into one of three subtypes:
Standard Zoan, Ancient Zoan, and Mythical Zoan are the three subtypes of zoan devil fruits that define a zoan user’s abilities and what creature they can transform into. Standard zoan subtypes are very common among zoan devil fruit users, whereas ancient and mythical zoans are incredibly rare and nearly impossible to find normally.
The subtype determines not only the creature into which the user can transform, but also the general power level and rarity of the fruit. Ancient and Mythical Zoans are much rarer and more powerful than Standard Zoans.

sections.name: Zoan Type: Standard
sections.text: Grants transformation into a common animal, such as a wolf, eagle, or elephant.

sections.name: Zoan Type: Ancient
sections.text: Grants transformation into prehistoric creatures, such as dinosaurs or mammoths.

sections.name: Zoan Type: Mythical
sections.text: Grants transformation into legendary beasts from fantasy, such as dragons or phoenixes, often with additional magical abilities.

sections.name: Human Form
sections.text:
Upon gaining Zoan powers, the user permanently increases one of their ability scores. Choose the highest ability score from the Beast Shape’s stat block; increase your matching score by half of the modifier of that ability, rounded up (up to a maximum of 20). For example, if your beast form has a +6 Strength modifier, and your current Strength is 10, your Strength becomes 13. This bonus can be further increased through ability score increases as normal when leveling up.
If there is more than one highest ability score you may choose the one you want.

sections.name: Transfer Ability Score Improvements
sections.text: When you gain any ability score improvements due to your class or by any other means, increase your Beast Form’s same ability scores by the amount you gain up to 30.

sections.name: Beast Form
sections.text:
As an action on your turn, you can transform into the beast designated by your Zoan Devil Fruit. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses at dawn.
You remain in Beast Form for a number of hours equal to half your character level (rounded up). You can revert to your normal form early by using a bonus action. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, become incapacitated by seastone or standing water, or drop to 0 hit points.
You cannot be in Beast Form and Hybrid Form at the same time.

sections.name: Beast Form Rules
sections.text:
When you transform, your physical body is entirely replaced by that of your Zoan beast. The following changes occur:
Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast Form’s statistics, except for your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.
You retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the Beast Form. You assume the Beast Form’s size, senses, movement speeds, natural weapons, and innate abilities, but you do not obtain its Legendary Actions. If your Beast Form’s size is smaller than your Human Form’s size, your Beast Form’s size is equal to your Human Form.
When you transform, your hit points become the Beast Form hit points (see Scaling Beast Form HP). When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren’t knocked unconscious.
You cannot cast spells or use your human form features while transformed unless a feature explicitly allows you to do so. However, you may use any haki features you have gained.
You retain the active or passive benefits of class features, race traits, and feats if your Beast Form is physically capable of using them.
Equipment either merges into your form or falls to the ground (your choice). Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature’s shape and size. Your equipment doesn’t change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can’t wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

sections.name: Beast Form HP and Damage Scaling
sections.text:
Zoan Beast Forms grow stronger as their users level up, following a structured scaling system based on the Devil Fruit’s rarity.
You use your Devil Fruit save DC to determine the DC of your beast form abilities, spells, and attacks.
If an attack or ability has multiple damage types in a single attack, use the numbers in parentheses in the Attack/Ability Damage Die column.

sections.name: Beast Form CR and Attack Dice Scaling
sections.text: For example, a Neko Neko no Mi: Model House Cat is an Uncommon Devil fruit. At Level 6, the character’s Beast Form would have 36 hit points (6x6) and deal 2d8 Slashing damage with its claw attack.

rows: Player Level Beast Shape CR Proficiency Bonus Attack Dice

sections.name: Hybrid Form
sections.text:
Using an action, a Zoan user can enter their Hybrid Form, blending their humanoid and beast traits into one formidable form. When entering Hybrid Form:
You gain an additional boost to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores equal to the corresponding modifiers in your Beast Form (positive modifiers only).
Your ability scores can temporarily exceed 20 but not beyond 30.
When you transform into your Hybrid Form you may choose to be any size between your Human Form and Beast Form’s sizes.
Hybrid Form lasts for a number of minutes equal to your character level or until you end it as a bonus action, are incapacitated, or fall unconscious. You may enter Hybrid Form a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining expended uses at dawn.

sections.name: Hybrid Form Options
sections.text:
When you enter your Hybrid Form, you gain access to an amount of Hybrid Form Options based on your character’s level.
Choose an amount of the following categories equal to your option amount above and gain a corresponding benefit based on your Zoan beast stat block:
Speed and Senses. You gain all of your beast form’s movement speeds (if they are higher than yours) and senses (ect. darkvision, tremorsense, truesight, ect).
Defenses and Vulnerabilities. You gain all of your beast form’s Damage Immunities, Resistances, and Vulnerabilities. You can not gain the beast form’s Condition Immunities.
Feature. You gain one of your beast form’s innate features. Consult your DM to determine whether the feature can function properly in your hybrid state.
Action. You may select one natural weapon or special action (Breath Weapon, Web, etc.) from your beast form and use it in your hybrid form using your own ability modifiers with the exception of multiattack which you cannot take. If the action requires a recharge or saving throw, it retains that restriction and DC scaling follows your character stats. Natural attacks are considered unarmed attacks when taken, and are proficient with them.

sections.name: No Remaining Hybrid Form Options?
sections.text: If you run out of hybrid form options on your beast stat block to choose from, you instead gain +2 to an ability score of your choice (Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution) per remaining Hybrid Form Option not used for the duration of your hybrid form.

sections.name: Awakened Form
sections.text: Upon Awakening, when a Zoan user transforms into their Hybrid Form, they can instead transform into a True OR Cursed Awakened Form of their choice. See the Legendary “Devil Fruit Spiritual Advancements” in Chapter 5: Spirit Surges for more information.

entries.name: Logia Rules
entries.text: Logia Devil Fruits are among the rarest and most powerful of all Devil Fruit types. They allow the user to transform into a natural element, control it freely, and even create it from their body. Unlike Paramecia or Zoan users, Logia users typically become completely intangible to physical harm, making them particularly difficult to damage or restrain without specialized techniques like Haki.

sections.name: Logia Subtypes
sections.text:
Logia Fruits are divided into three primary subtypes based on the physical state of their associated element:
Solid Logias, Liquid Logias, and Gaseous Logias are the three subtypes of logia devil fruits that define a logia user’s abilities and what element and state of matter they can transform into or use with their powers. All three of these subtypes are roughly equal in power, though some logia elements can be weaker than others on average.

sections.name: Logia Type: Solid
sections.text: Users transform into and manipulate solid substances, such as ice, metal, or stone.

sections.name: Logia Type: Liquid
sections.text: Users become and control a liquid substance like magma, oil, or mud. Liquid fresh water or sea water cannot be used as a logia element.

sections.name: Logia Type: Gaseous
sections.text: Users embody a gaseous or plasma-like substance, such as smoke, lightning, or fire.

sections.name: Special Logia Type: Darkness
sections.text:
The Yami Yami no Mi, or darkness logia, is such a unique and powerful devil fruit that it deserves its own subcategory. Unlike other logias, its user cannot disperse into darkness or avoid physical attacks. However, it gives the user complete control over darkness that they can produce, which can consume any material or element.
While each subtype shares common rules, they also gain unique movement capabilities and resistances based on their physical state.

sections.name: Elemental Traits and Immunities
sections.text:
Upon consuming a Logia Fruit, a user gains complete control over their respective element. They gain immunity to all nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, as well as elemental resistance or immunity aligned with their form (e.g., fire for a flame user, cold for an ice user). Users also become immune to any condition or damage source that logically wouldn’t affect their element.
For instance, a smoke user might ignore effects like choking gases or suffocation, while a lightning user may move at impossible speeds and bypass traditional movement restrictions.
Magical or Haki-infused attacks still bypass resistances, making such threats essential for balancing encounters.

sections.name: Basic Ability
sections.text: Each Logia Fruit grants an always-available ability, often mimicking a cantrip or a physical trait of the element. This ability should reflect the fruit’s nature and provide tactical utility.

sections.name: Spellcasting and Charge Progression
sections.text:
Logia users cast spells using a pool of Devil Fruit charges that scale with level. They can choose spells from any spell list that match their elemental flavor. All spells cast using the Devil Fruit consume charges equal to the spell’s level and can be upcast by spending additional charges.
All Logia users must replace the damage type of their Devil Fruit spells with one matching their element. Spells and Features ignore damage resistances unless the material in question has a specific counter-property (such as rubber resisting electricity).

sections.name: Logia Charge Scaling
sections.text: For example, the Gin Gin no Mi (Silver) can cast 1st level Heat Metal for 1 charges. A level 5 character can upcast the spell to a max of 4th level for a cost of 4 charges.

sections.name: Elemental Form
sections.text:
Upon mastering their Logia powers, the user learns to fully embody their elemental nature. As an action, you can transform into a being of pure element, entering your Elemental Form. This form is distinct for each subtype: Solid, Liquid, or Gaseous, and provides unique advantages based on the physical state of your element.
Some Logia Devil Fruits span multiple subtypes. For example, a silver user may count as both liquid and solid, or a soot user might count as solid and gaseous. If your Devil Fruit qualifies for more than one elemental subtype, you may choose which form to enter each time you activate your Elemental Form. You may not change the form while it is active.
You can remain in your Elemental Form for a number of minutes equal to half your character level (rounded up). You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all uses upon completing a long rest. If you are incapacitated, fall unconscious, or are exposed to seastone or submerged in water, the form ends immediately.
Worn equipment functions as usual, but benefits from your resistances and immunities and attacks that normally phase through you will also phase through your equipment as if it is a part of your body.
Additionally, your Devil Fruit spells are cast with -1 devil fruit charge while you are in your elemental form and your ignore damage immunities, causing the target to take half of the damage dealt instead unless the target in question has a specific counter-property (such as rubber resisting electricity).

sections.name: Solid Elemental Form
sections.text:
Your body becomes a cohesive mass of solid matter, such as ice, glass, or stone. You can shatter and reform at will.
While in this form, you gain a +4 bonus to AC. Once per turn, as a bonus action or a reaction to taking damage, you may disperse and reform within 30 feet of your current space, reappearing in a burst of shards or fragments.
Your melee attacks are treated as magical and deal bonus damage equal to half your level (rounded down).
You gain advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.
You can move through objects made of the same element as you. If you end your turn inside of an object, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you occupied, and you take 1d8 force damage.

sections.name: Liquid Elemental Form
sections.text:
You liquefy entirely, your body shifting into a flowing, adaptable substance.
You gain resistance to fire damage, and you can squeeze through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
Your melee attack range increases by 15 ft.
Once per round, You can spend 5 feet of movement to transform into your liquid element and move into the small cracks of a solid surface and reform in a puddle, reappearing on a spot on the same surface up to 30 feet away from you that you don’t need to be able to see.
You are immune to nonmagical restraints or grapples.
You can choose to leave behind a trail of your logia’s liquid, which lasts until the start of your next turn and is considered difficult terrain.
You can move through the space of another creature, and it doesn’t count as difficult terrain. If you end your turn in another creature’s space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you occupied, and you take 1d8 force damage.

sections.name: Gaseous Elemental Form
sections.text:
Your form disperses into vapor, mist, plasma, or particulate energy.
You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover effortlessly.
Your melee attack range increases by 10 ft.
You can pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks. You remain hovering in the air even when stunned or otherwise Incapacitated, unless by seastone or water.
You are immune to nonmagical restraints or grapples.
While in this form, you have advantage on Dexterity saving throws and Stealth checks, and ranged weapon attacks against you are made with disadvantage.
You can move through the space of another creature, and it doesn’t count as difficult terrain. If you end your turn in another creature’s space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you occupied, and you take 1d8 force damage.

sections.name: Awakening
sections.text: Once awakened, Logia users transcend their normal boundaries and permanently affect the environment around them. This ability is often unique to the fruit. Examples include a snow user creating a permanent blizzard zone or a flame user igniting the terrain they walk on.

entries.name: Devil Fruit Appraisal
entries.text: Devil Fruits are among the rarest treasures in the world, each containing a unique supernatural power. Their unpredictable nature makes them objects of wonder, fear, and immense value. Correctly identifying one can be the difference between gaining a priceless weapon or wasting a fortune.

sections.name: Identification
sections.text:
Every Devil Fruit shares the iconic swirling patterns across its skin, though its color, shape, and markings often hint at its category (Paramecia, Zoan, or Logia). However, the true power of a Devil Fruit cannot be confirmed until it is consumed.
Rare texts known as Devil Fruit Encyclopedias contain illustrations and descriptions of many known fruits, but these books are nearly as rare and costly as Legendary fruits themselves. Outside of these tomes, most buyers must rely on skilled appraisers or risky Underworld services.

sections.name: Magic and Devil Fruits
sections.text: Devil Fruits resist conventional magic. Standard identification spells and divinations cannot reveal their nature unless explicitly stated. This innate supernatural resistance preserves their mystery and prevents easy exploitation.

sections.name: Appraisal
sections.text: A Devil Fruit may be appraised by a skilled expert, though finding one is extremely difficult. Even a capable appraiser has only a 50% chance of correctly identifying a fruit’s category and general abilities. If successful, the service carries a steep price depending on the fruit’s rarity.

sections.name: Devil Fruit Appraisal Fee
sections.text: In addition, an ability analysis fee of ฿10,000,000 is charged to reveal the exact powers and category of the fruit, if possible.
